DEC-recover_then_compare.title: Branch · SUN Model Discussion
DEC-recover_then_compare.exact_quote:
1. **Recover the existing SUN derivation.** Inspect the earlier records for its actual rules and original 70/72 proof. Mark anything unrecovered explicitly.
2. **Compare that derivation with the musical evidence.** Record which relationships it explains, which contradict it, and which remain unresolved.
3. **Finish qualifying candidate generators.** Determine from sources what each candidate does, where it applies, and whether it generates anything.
4. **Prove the remaining equivalences and compositions.** Establish which candidates are interchangeable and which can be constructed from others, preserving necessary distinctions.
5. **Derive the alphabet.** Reduce the qualified candidates to a sufficient generating set and prove any claimed minimality.
6. **Finish the generative hypergraph.** Record how those generators produce the supported relationships.
7. **Run downstream certification.** Test the resulting system and comparison cases; report actual passes, failures, and unresolved results.
8. **Save the finished result and update this checklist.**

**Current position:** the evidence map and several local proofs are complete. The unified generating system is unfinished. The historical **70/72 result remains recorded as established; its original proof trace remains unrecovered.**
DEC-recover_then_compare.host_retrieval_label: Recover the existing derivation before deriving the alphabet and graph.

DEC-dont_ontologize_judges.title: Branch · SUN Model Discussion
DEC-dont_ontologize_judges.exact_quote:
Yes. Checked against the current governed artifacts, this is the cleaner architecture.
The important correction is even stronger than “Shem is not Judge B”: **“Judge A / Judge B” should not be ontologized at all.** In the current workbook, judging is an evaluation procedure. Tree, Yetzirah, music, and Shem are candidate objects with different native functions. Turning two of them into permanent judges conflates the test harness with the systems being tested.
Historically, your distinction is also sound. *Shem ha-Meforash* is an older term for the distinguished/divine Name and is used for the Tetragrammaton in tannaitic material; the familiar later 72-fold construction is a more specific development. [Jewish Encyclopedia](https://www.jewishencyclopedia.com/articles/13542-shem-ha-meforash?utm_source=chatgpt.com) The 72-fold construction takes three 72-letter verses from Exodus 14:19–21, reverses the middle row, and reads corresponding positions to form 72 triplets. [Chabad](https://www.chabad.org/kabbalah/article_cdo/aid/1388270/jewish/72-Names-of-G-d.htm?utm_source=chatgpt.com) *Sefer
DEC-dont_ontologize_judges.host_retrieval_label: Judge A/Judge B are not independent ontological objects.
